chunks: And from him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), [regarding] the saying of Allah, the Exalted, in His Book: "That is for he whose family was not present in the Sacred Mosque."

He said, "He means the people of Mecca. There is no Mut'ah upon them. Everyone whose family is within eight and forty miles, from source to source, and 'Usfan, as it circles around Mecca, is among those included in this verse. And everyone whose family is beyond that, upon him is the Mut'ah."

key_terms.ذَاتَ عِرْقٍ: From source to source (referring to the extent of the area)
key_terms.عُسْفَانُ: 'Usfan (a place near Mecca marking the boundary)
key_terms.مُتْعَةٌ: Mut'ah (a type of pilgrimage with specific conditions)

ai.seo_question: What is the distance limit for exemption from Mut'ah pilgrimage according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies the geographical scope of the exemption from *Mut'at al-Hajj* (temporary pilgrimage) mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah. He specifies that residents within a radius of 84 miles from Mecca to 'Usfan are exempt, while those beyond this boundary are obligated to perform the full Hajj with *Tamattu'*. This ruling establishes a clear jurisprudential boundary for distinguishing between local Meccans and pilgrims from distant regions.
